brief.headline: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom
bullets: Private Credit: Private credit is gaining ground in Asia as demand for flexible capital grows and the AI boom needs funding, according to KKR.
Real Estate: Gaylord Rockies in Aurora plans a $305M expansion with 450 rooms and a luxury indoor water park, boosting group travel and events.

M&A & Buyouts: Private equity firm TPG has agreed to acquire financial software provider BILL Holdings in partnership with Corpay in an all-cash take-private valued at about $6bn, according to a report by Reuters.
Investor Outlook: Barry speaks with David Eichhorn, CEO and Head of Investment Strategies at NISA Investment Advisors.
Hotels & Hospitality: Diriyah has canceled a $191 million hotel contract and won’t say why.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: signals are mixed, with some markets calm and others showing strain, so expect selective risk-taking. The S&P 500 stands at 7,175.83 (down 2.0% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 28.4, an elevated reading that signals nervous markets. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.04% (down 3 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.29 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.52%, near long-run norms (up 5 bps on the prior reading).
